data.text:
Manila Mayor @IskoMoreno criticized activists who spray-painted slogans on the Lagusnilad Underpass during the International Women's Day protest on March 8, saying the act damaged public infrastructure and will require city resources to repair.

Domagoso raised the issue during the city’s March 9 flag-raising ceremony at Kartilya ng Katipunan, where he pointed to the graffiti left on the walls of the underpass, an area recently cleaned by the Manila city government.

The mayor said the vandalism would require the city to purchase paint and deploy workers from the engineering office and the Department of Public Services to repaint the affected sections. He noted that manpower that could otherwise be assigned to other public service tasks would instead be redirected to restore the underpass.

City officials have begun repainting the damaged sections of the Lagusnilad Underpass following the protest.

WORKERS DEMAND WAGE HIKE, OIL TAX RELIEF AMID CRISIS

The Kilusan ng Manggagawa (KMU) led a protest in Recto, Manila, calling for an end to the US-Israel war in Iran, citing risks to the lives and livelihoods of Filipinos, particularly the more than 2 million Overseas Filipino Workers (OFW) in the Middle East.

Protesters urged President Bongbong Marcos to implement urgent measures to support households facing rising oil prices and worsening economic conditions.

Among their demands were raising the national minimum wage to PHP 1,200 and removing the 12% Value-Added Tax and excise taxes on oil to ease the burden on workers and consumers.

📸 Jonas Sulit, Abante
